candidates.title: CN 3Q profit rises 6% as freight revenue climbs
candidates.excerpt: Canadian National Railway reported a 6% increase in third-quarter profit Friday as stronger grain, energy and automotive freight activity lifted revenue, while higher fuel costs and a technology write-down weighed on reported margins. The Montreal-based railway (NYSE: CNI) maintained its full-year earnings outlook, saying growth was tracking toward the upper end of its forecast range. CN earned C$1.209 billion ($866 million), or $1.43 per diluted share, in the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with $816 million, or $1.31 a share, a year earlier. Revenue increased 15% to $3.42 billion from $2.98 billion. Adjusted diluted earnings rose 18% to approximately $1.55 a share, excluding a software impairment and rail-merger-related advisory expenses. That exceeded analysts’ expectations of about $1.50 a share, according to FactSet figures reported by Dow Jones. Revenue also topped the approximately $3.34 billion forecast. candidates.title: Schneider to shift eastern rail business to Norfolk Southern from CSX
candidates.excerpt: Schneider will make Norfolk Southern its primary eastern rail provider under an agreement announced Oct. 29 aimed at expanding domestic intermodal capacity and giving shippers more options to move freight across the eastern United States. The agreement, effective in November, shifts Schneider’s NYSE: SNDR) company-owned equipment, drivers and logistics operations away from CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) and pairs it with Norfolk Southern’s 22-state intermodal network. The companies said the partnership would expand market access, increase capacity flexibility and help attract freight now moving by truck. “As we transition our primary eastern rail provider to Norfolk Southern, we’ll expand access to key markets, increase network flexibility and create new opportunities to better serve our customers,” said Michael Baumgardt, Schneider’s executive vice president of intermodal and logistics, in a release. candidates.title: Union Pacific dispatchers to vote on unionization
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — The National Mediation Board has formally authorized a representational election for Union Pacific dispatchers, which will determine if they will organize under the American Train Dispatchers Association, the union announced on Thursday, Oct. 29. In a press release, the ATDA called the authorization a “significant milestone” in an organizing campaign within the ranks of UP dispatchers, saying it represents months of effort “despite the challenges inherent in organizing a workforce of this size.” The union said it will provide whatever support and resources the dispatchers need. The ATDA, founded in 1917 in Spokane, Wash., is affiliated with the Transportation Trades Department of the AFL-CIO. It has about 2,700 members. candidates.title: CN reports stronger third-quarter profits
candidates.excerpt: MONTREAL — Canadian National’s profits rose in the third quarter as the railway handled more tonnage and notched productivity and efficiency gains. “This was another solid quarter. We moved more freight while maintaining a fluid network and translated that volume growth into higher earnings and free cash flow,” CEO Tracy Robinson said on the railway’s Friday morning earnings call. Quarterly operating income increased 8%, to $1.33 billion U.S., as revenue rose 15%, to $3.41 billion. Earnings per share grew 9%, to $1.43. CN’s operating ratio was 63.7%, a 2.3-point increase from a year ago, as expenses rose 18%, led by a 56% increase in fuel costs. Robinson said CN has delivered $120 million worth of productivity and efficiency gains this year, and that its “boots on the ground” sales efforts have generated $300 million in revenue to help offset the impact of U.S. tariffs and trade tensions. candidates.title: India approves major container manufacturing support scheme
candidates.excerpt: India’s Union Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme, a Rs 10,000 crore programme designed to expand domestic production and reduce the country’s reliance on imported shipping containers. According to two official government announcements, the programme will run from the 2027-28 financial year until 2039-40. It will support new manufacturing plants and the expansion of existing facilities. The Indian government aims to increase annual container manufacturing capacity almost tenfold. Capacity is expected to rise from approximately 70,000 TEU today to 750,000 TEU. The programme was initially announced as part of India’s Union Budget for 2026-27. Support for new and existing factories The scheme includes Rs 859 crore of interest support. Eligible manufacturers will receive a 3% annual interest subsidy on term loans used for new factories or capacity expansions. candidates.title: Maersk introduces reefer surcharge for shipments to Tema
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will introduce a Peak Season Surcharge (PSS) for refrigerated cargo moving from the Far East, Middle East and Americas to Tema, Ghana. The surcharge will take effect on 16 November 2026. For regulated countries, it will apply from 1 December 2026. The surcharge will remain applicable until further notice. For non-SPOT bookings, Maersk will determine the rate using the Price Calculation Date. For non-FMC shipments, this is the scheduled departure date of the first water leg at booking confirmation. For FMC shipments, the PCD is the final container gate-in date. The surcharge does not apply to SPOT bookings. Maersk will collect the charge according to the freight payment terms. Other applicable local and contingency surcharges may also apply.

candidates.excerpt: Soaring tanker freight rates are taking an increasingly heavy toll on the world’s oil majors, with the latest quarterly results revealing billions of dollars in additional shipping-related liabilities, squeezed refining margins and losses on trading positions. Shell has disclosed a $5.4bn non-cash increase in its shipping lease liabilities during the third quarter, reflecting the extraordinary rise in tanker rates since the outbreak of the Middle East conflict. The accounting adjustment relates to index-linked vessel charters, which must be revalued using prevailing spot rates. Shell’s shipping lease liabilities have increased by nearly $7.7bn since the beginning of the year, although the company stressed that the revaluations do not represent immediate cash expenditure. candidates.excerpt: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators Kroll and StepStone Group have launched three new payment-in-kind (PIK) indicators to provide greater transparency into the use of non-cash interest in private credit markets. The indicators form part of the firms’ private credit benchmarks, covering more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data dating back to 2012. They measure PIK as a proportion of interest income, the percentage of loans with an active PIK component by deal count, and their share of outstanding principal. The indicators will also allow investors to compare PIK usage across geographies, sectors and borrower sizes. The launch comes as the firms’ data suggests PIK usage is moderating, with non-cash interest accounting for 2.86 per cent of interest income on loans originated globally over the previous 12 months, as of 10 October 2026. candidates.title: First look: CPKC earnings
candidates.excerpt: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported a 16% increase in third-quarter core adjusted earnings per share Wednesday, as higher freight volumes and growth in grain and intermodal revenue helped offset rising fuel costs. Revenue rose to C$4.22 billion ($3.01 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from $2.61 billion a year earlier, the Calgary-based company (NYSE: CP) said in earnings released after the close of markets. Core adjusted diluted earnings increased to 91 cents per share from 78 cents, while reported diluted earnings rose 3% to 74 cents from 72 cents. candidates.title: Greenbrier profit falls as railcar demand weighs on sales
candidates.excerpt: Greenbrier Cos. reported a sharp decline in quarterly profit and revenue as the freight-railcar manufacturer contended with weaker demand and facility-related costs. The Lake Oswego, Ore., company (NYSE: GBX) saw an increase in its order backlog and growth in its leasing fleet amid improving business conditions. The company said Monday that net earnings attributable to Greenbrier fell to $8.7 million, or 27 cents a diluted share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Aug. 31, from $36.8 million, or $1.16 a share, a year earlier. Revenue declined 22% to $591 million from $759.5 million. Excluding facility-rationalization costs, core earnings were 39 cents a share. The charges reduced quarterly earnings by 12 cents a share after tax and non-controlling interests. Revenue fell short of analysts’ expectations of about $605 million, while core earnings missed the 80-cent analysts’ consensus of MarketBeat. Police recover $54K in Hot Wheels after BNSF freight train burglary in California
candidates.excerpt: Police recovered approximately $54,000 in stolen Hot Wheels merchandise following a freight train burglary in Colton, California. A witness called 911 around 3 a.m. Thursday, October 22, reporting suspicious activity near railroad tracks. Officers spotted a black Chevrolet Silverado leaving the area and initiated a traffic stop. The investigation ended with one arrest and 350 boxes of toy cars in police custody. According to video released by the Colton Police Department, the caller reported people stealing merchandise near Maple Street. An officer positioned himself near Seventh Street and La Cadena Drive while monitoring the surrounding roads. Footage shows authorities following the pickup before stopping its driver. The man exited with his hands on his head, and officers took him into custody. The department confirmed the recovery in its October 22 Facebook announcement.
